evidence.title: Cipher Mining Signs Additional 56 MW, 10-Year AI Hosting Agreement with Fluidstack
evidence.excerpt: Cipher reports an additional 39 MW of critical IT load supported by a maximum of 56 MW of additional gross capacity at Barber Lake in Colorado City, increasing Fluidstack's lease to the entire 300 MW site.

metadata.capacity_scope: The release reports 56 MW of additional gross capacity supporting 39 MW of additional critical IT load. They are two metrics for the same Phase II component, not additive megawatts.
metadata.capacity_stage_scope: Delivery was prospective, so both rows are retained as planned capacity despite the agreement being contracted. Neither is current draw or measured consumption.

metadata.site_end_state_scope: The release says Fluidstack will lease the entire 300 MW Barber Lake site after the additional agreement. The 300 MW is the gross site end state, not a value additional to the 244 MW and 56 MW components.

metadata.google_context: The release discusses an incremental Google financial backstop. That backstop is not a tenant, customer, user, operator, developer, owner, or workload claim.

evidence.title: Cipher Digital Inc. 2025 Form 10-K
evidence.excerpt: Cipher's Form 10-K describes the 300 MW gross Barber Lake Facility near Colorado City, allocated as 244 MW Phase I and 56 MW Phase II, and the separate 300 gross MW Black Pearl AWS lease near Wink with retrofit and development commenced in 2025.
